([[Dnipropetrovsk, Ukraine]]) | college = [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] (2011–2013) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = 2010 | career_end = | years1 = 2010–2011 | team1 = [[BC Dnipro]] ([[Ukrainian Basketball Superleague|Ukraine]]) | years2 = | team2 = | highlights = | stat1label = | stat1value = | stat2label = | stat2value = | stat3label = | stat3value = | letter = | bbr = | HOF_player = | FIBA_HOF_player = }} '''Alex Len''' ({{lang-uk|Олексій Лен}}, ''Oleksiy Len''; born June 16, 1993) is a Ukrainian [[basketball]] center who declared his eligibility for the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. Before declaring for the draft, he played two seasons with the [[NCAA]]'s [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. ==Early life== Len was born in [[Antratsyt]], [[Ukraine]]http://www.eurohopes.com/player/1429/olexiy-len/, where he grew up as a gymnast because he liked [[Jackie Chan]] movies. He started playing basketball at the age of 13. He attended Dnipropetrovsk Higher College in [[Dnipropetrovsk]], [[Ukraine]].http://www.nbadraft.net/players/alex-len He was a standout for the Ukraine national team at the [[2010 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. ==University of Maryland== He was the recipient of an athletic scholarship from the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] coach [[Gary Williams]], but Williams resigned after the 2010-11 season, leading to [[Mark Turgeon]] to take his place. While Williams began recruiting Len, it was [http://maryland.247sports.com/Article/Maryland-Adds-7-foot-2-Ukranian-Star-Oleksiy-Len-35896 Turgeon who eventually lured him to Maryland.] Len underachieved in his freshman year, averaging 6 PPG, 5.4 RPG, and 2.1 BPG, but showed lottery pick potential after serving a ten game suspension at the beginning of the year due to NCAA amateurism issues resulting from his play with [[BC Dnipro|BC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk]], a European club team from his home nation. Len opened his sophomore season on November 9, 2012 against the reigning champion [[Kentucky Wildcats]], led by ESPN's #1 player of the 2012 recruiting class, [[Nerlens Noel]].{{cite web|author=Nerlens Noel |url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/97363/nerlens-noel |title=Basketball Recruiting - Nerlens Noel - Player Profiles - ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2012-11-26}} The game was played at the brand new [[Barclays Center]] in [[Brooklyn, New York]]. Len overpowered Noel throughout the entire game, scoring 23 points with 12 rebounds and 4 blocks, while holding Noel to 4 points, 9 rebounds, and 3 blocks, although Kentucky won the game 72-69. Following the game, there was talk that Len could potentially be a top 5 pick in the upcoming draft. On January 16, 2013, Len ended up scoring 10 points and grabbed 6 rebounds, including a game-winning shot with 0.9 seconds in the game, to get a 51-50 upset over #14 [[North Carolina State Wolfpack men's basketball|North Carolina State]]. On February 16, 2013, Len again played a starring role, leading Maryland to an 83-81 upset victory over the top ranked [[Duke Blue Devils]]. He is currently projected to land in the lottery.{{cite web|title=Terps' Alex Len to enter NBA draft |url=http://www.baltimorenewsjournal.com/2013/04/15/terps-alex-len-to-enter-nba-draft/|work=BaltimoreNewsJournal.com|accessdate=April 15, 2013}} On May 3, 2013, Len ended up getting surgery on his ankle that resulted in him being out for around 4-6 months.http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9239845/alex-len-miss-all-pre-draft-workouts-surgery ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://247sports.com/Player/Alex-Len-19155 247Sports.com] *[http://www.nbadraft.net/players/alex-len Nbadraft.net] *[http://www.alexlen.com Alexlen.com] *[http://www.umterps.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/len_alex00.html Umterps.com] *[http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/57379/alex-len Espn.go.com] *[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_KNce8jInH7Qj1EsyH5rjn2.playerID_75836.compID_8aYeHlfuGF-mF5IqO8aFH1.season_2010.roundID_7323.teamID_2183.html 2010 FIBA U-18 profile] {{Persondata | NAME = Len, Alex | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = Basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = June 16, 1993 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Antratsyt, Ukraine | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Len, Alex}} [[Category:1993 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Maryland Terrapins men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Antratsyt]] [[Category:Ukrainian basketball players]] [[Category:Ukrainian expatriate basketball people in the United States]]
